summary: Nineteen messages, 7 of them from Alanna — her highest volume in five weeks and a sharp reversal of last week's 'she stopped asking' reading. But the re-engagement arrived as the first explicit complaint of the relationship. On 9/23 Mica Vecco posted a fifth request to upload content to ALTR's Google Drive; on 9/24 at 17:24 Alanna answered in capitals — 'Guys for the millionth time I HAVE MY OWN DRIVE AND DROPBOX', followed by 'I’m not uploading to yours!! Why would I, I have 5000 + videos in my own that I have already organised' — and then tagged '@ofwizz' to escalate. Derrek replied three minutes later and reversed the policy in two lines ('yes we can easily do this', 'makes 0 difference to us'), Mica folded immediately and well ('yeah we can pull from your drives', 'just didn’t have them here, apologies!'), and a 38-day content blocker closed inside four minutes. That is the week in one exchange: the fix was always trivial, nobody senior looked at it for five weeks, and it took the client shouting and tagging the owner to get it. Derrek's three messages were his first in this chat in 43 days. On money the situation got materially worse and, for the first time, mechanically stuck. Stephski chased invoice #3 on 9/21 ahead of its due date with a specific reference — 'Tomorrow is day 7 since recieving invoice' — and Alanna responded on 9/22 by volunteering the phone number Stephski had asked for on 9/3 and requesting the Zelle: 'Hey can you Zelle request me on [REDACTED-NUMBER] it’s not working for me'. She was trying to pay. Twenty-one hours later, after Mayson had to tag '@stephskiii' to surface it, the answer was 'can you please do it as a wire instead of zelle it wont work for some reason' — pushing her back to the exact rail she had just said was failing. Nobody connected that failure to the payee name change announced inside the invoice #3 message on 9/15 ('a slight name change to the account... This should help alleviate any bounce backs'), which is the single most likely cause of a wire not going through. Net result at window close: invoice #2 (Aug 15-31) is 17 days past ALTR's own term, 24 days from issue and has not been named by anyone since 9/5 — twenty days; invoice #3 (Sept 1-14) is now also past due as of 9/22; two invoices are outstanding, nothing has been collected since 8/30, and invoice #4 is due to issue around 10/1, which would make three concurrent. Meanwhile the service she actually pays for produced nothing at all: Ollie Mckinlay sent zero messages, is 11 days silent and has contributed three words in 24 days; the 5000+ photos she handed over on 9/10 are 15 days unacknowledged; her release calendar has been empty for 27 days; Michelle sent zero messages and is 14 days silent, so the new Instagram account promised on 9/1 and 'ready in a few days' on 9/10 has had no update in 15 days. Mayson opened a fifth orphaned ask ('Hey @alannaapow are you available to hop on a call today?', 9/22, unanswered). She still supplied content unprompted on 9/24 — three more library links — and outside the one outburst her tone did not change.

health.rationale: Down 4 from 49. Two things moved in opposite directions and the money decided it. The genuine good news: the 38-day content blocker is closed, Derrek fixed it in four minutes on 9/24, Mica reversed and apologised inside two minutes, and the client re-engaged hard — 7 messages against 3 last week, with real asks in them. The reason the score still falls: she had to shout to get it. 'Guys for the millionth time I HAVE MY OWN DRIVE AND DROPBOX' and 'I’m not uploading to yours!! Why would I' are the first expressions of frustration in 53 days from a client who had previously complained about nothing, and she routed them past the account team to the owner handle. A client who escalates is a client who has stopped believing the normal channel works. On money the account is now not just late but mechanically stuck: she volunteered her phone number and asked for a Zelle request on 9/22 — she was actively trying to pay — waited 21 hours and a third-party tag for a reply, and was told ALTR's Zelle 'wont work for some reason' and to use a wire, which is what she had just said was not working for her. The payee name change announced inside invoice #3 on 9/15 is the obvious suspect and nobody has tested it. Invoice #2 is 17 days past term, 24 days from issue and 20 days unmentioned by anyone; invoice #3 went past its own 9/22 due date inside this window; two invoices are open, one payment has been collected in the account's history and it took 15 days, four chases and a work-stoppage threat. Invoice #4 issues around 10/1. Against that, the core service was a complete no-show for a fourth cycle: Ollie zero messages and 11 days silent, three words in 24 days, nine commitments untouched, the 5000+ photo handover 15 days unanswered, the release calendar 27 days empty on her stated number-one priority. Michelle zero messages and 14 days silent with the new Instagram account 15 days past its own soft deadline. The chatter FAQ form is 53 days old and was last chased 51 days ago. What holds the score above 40 is real: the blocker closed, the owner engaged, Mica recovered gracefully, Stephski chased ahead of a due date rather than after it, Mayson relayed the payment request within ten hours, and the client is still producing and still sending content unprompted. What pushes it down is that the client's patience became visible this week, and the only thing standing between her and the exit is a payment she cannot currently make.
